stories.headline: St. Louis up to 2nd place with unbeaten run now at 17 games
stories.summary: Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.

St. Louis (13-6-8) extended its unbeaten streak to 17 matches in MLS play and moved up to second place in MLS' Western Conference table.

New York (9-12-6) entered having conceded just two goals in its last four games, with Ethan Horvath recording three shutouts.

The Red Bulls had won their last two games, but were without rising stars Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall for the game, with the pair away on national team duty for the United States.

Rafael Navarro opened the scoring just five minutes into the game when he redirected Conrad Wallem's header across the goal.

Becher capitalized on a New York turnover deep in its own half to make it 2-0 in the 87th minute. Ostrak sent in a rebound in stoppage time.

Roman Bürki made four saves to earn his third clean sheet of the season for St. Louis.

It was the first time New York and St. Louis have met during the regular season.

St. Louis hosts the LA Galaxy next on Oct. 11, while the Red Bulls play San Diego FC at home the day before.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Ivan: Nathan Cleary can get even better after Dally M
stories.summary: Ivan Cleary has spoken of the horror of watching his son Nathan's leg injury, and a belief he can still get better again after winning his first Dally M.
stories.body:
Ivan Cleary has admitted watching his son Nathan suffer a badly broken leg marked one of the hardest days of his career, feeling the line between father and coach blurred for the first time.

But the veteran Penrith mentor is insistent his son Nathan still has more levels to attain once he returns from his injury, following his landmark Dally M victory on Wednesday night.

Cleary's Dally M triumph completed the Penrith halfback's rugby league box set, having now claimed every major team and individual honour available to him by age 28.

Unable to attend in person after being released from hospital following emergency surgery on his leg, the Panthers halfback collected the game's top honour while in a wheelchair at home.

Coach Ivan also appeared emotional during Nathan's pre-recorded speech, after the trophy was hand-delivered to the halfback earlier in the day.

"His voice perked up from what it's been the past couple of days," Ivan told AAP.

"It's a pretty amazing award. You don't play the game for individual awards, but it's certainly nice to be recognised.

"Particularly this award, it's pretty much the No.1 award in the game."

Reminded that his son had now scaled virtually every possible mountain in the sport, the Penrith coach insisted there were still improvements left in his son's game.

"It's crazy," Ivan said.

"I know he'd say it and I probably think a bit the same. You don't reflect too much when it's still going on. But when you put it like that, it's amazing.

"But I know there is so much more to come as well, and I know he thinks that way as well."

Nathan has received positive early news from surgeons after the operation on his compound fracture and dislocated ankle, as a result of a hip-drop tackle in Sunday's preliminary-final loss to Newcastle.

He will soon undergo surgery on other foot after fighting through a broken bone to play the Knights, but Penrith are hopeful he will be right for round one in 2027.

"Sunday was definitely one of the harder days I have been through," coach Cleary said.

"It's the first time where the line of dad and coach got a bit blurred. And the loss, I guess we have had a lot of good days so you can't have it all your way.

"Very emotional, but life goes on."

Footage has also emerged of fullback Dylan Edwards not only being horrified by the graphic injury at first, but then also trying to stop Nathan from seeing it.

"I was just trying to keep him calm as I could," Edwards said.

"To his credit he is a tough person. And the way he was handling that was incredible.

"It was gut-wrenching, something you're not used to seeing on the footy field."

Edwards, meanwhile, is still hopeful of being able to represent Australia at the World Cup after avoiding knee surgery following a PCL injury in the loss.

"I'm not sure, I have to talk to Kevvie (coach Kevin Walters)," Edwards said, while wearing a brace at the Dally Ms.

stories.headline: Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more
stories.summary: Tuesday's news that the Premier League found Man City guilty of 100-plus charges of breaking financial rules is a landmark moment. But what comes next: what punishments are on the table, and how does the appeals process work?
stories.body:
Manchester City's guilty verdict on 114 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules is a landmark moment in global sport.

City continues to assert their innocence and have signaled their intention to appeal before Friday's deadline. But the Independent Commission's verdict could hardly have been more damning, accusing the club of "sham" contracts involving its Abu Dhabi owners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" that contributed to inflating revenues and reducing costs by over £900 million. Witnesses in City's defense were accused of dishonesty, and the club was found to have "clearly intended to circumvent" Premier League rules.

The breaches relate specifically to a nine-year period (2009-18), but the shockwaves permeate far beyond. Pep Guardiola's trophy-laden legacy is in doubt. The Premier League's reputation and viability is in the balance. Rivals may seek retribution through compensation claims, triggering challenges that could last for years.

Meanwhile, City's punishment is yet to be determined. Under Section W, Rule 54 of the Premier League's Handbook, they are facing a punishment ranging from a reprimand to expulsion. There could be a fine, a points deduction and a transfer ban.

City's aggressive protestations of innocence only contribute to the widespread uncertainty and reduces the likelihood of all parties coming together to reach agreement on a settlement for the time being. Beyond that, the legal complexities are vast.

ESPN has spoken with one of the United Kingdom's leading law firms, Howard Kennedy, in pursuit of clarity. Partners Kyle Phillips and Lois Langton head the firm's sports group, with Phillips specializing in business crime and regulatory process. On Thursday, the pair talked with ESPN's James Olley to answer some basic questions and follow-ups about what this all means and what's next.

Editor's note: This interview has been edited for clarity and length.

How would you characterize the commission's findings?

Kyle Phillips: I think it's worse than many people expected. The words that were used by the commission in the findings report, caveated with the fact it's very difficult to read because a lot of it is redacted and there's no evidence or appendices that they keep referring to, but the language that they use is very strong.

"Sham" is one point. You've got the disguised payments, sorry -- the "disguised funding scheme," overstating commercial revenue, the amounts involved ... it is all quite shocking. And it is quite a strong statement to say that you find the witness evidence that was given to be "dishonest" -- a powerful word in any decision.

In any regulatory proceedings, it takes a lot for them to use that word.

How deliberate is this language? Are they effectively trying to preempt or dissuade an appeal?

Phillips: Although the panel's names are redacted, you'd expect them to be experienced lawyers. They would be quite cautious about their language and very deliberate in what they say. So you'd expect whatever they say to be thoroughly thought through. It's taken them three years to draft this and if they have come to that conclusion, to put it in this document...

The other angle is if they use such language and it's not supported by evidence, then it does open up grounds for appeal. There will be a fuller balanced judgment that we don't have sight of: that's the problem, so we can't assess the language that's used from that perspective. But you would think everything they said is supported somewhere by their evidential findings, and that they have got good grounds for making the points that they have.

Lois Langton: Every paragraph felt as though it'd been very carefully worded to try and limit the scope of any inevitable appeal. They must have recognized that Man City would want to do that.

And yet City continue to assert their innocence, citing their 'irrefutable evidence.' This requires a degree of speculation, but at what point are they going to produce this? There are suggestions they will argue that the Abu Dhabi government topped up the sponsorship and not the owners.

Phillips: I would expect that evidence to have already been presented, but reading between the lines -- and this is difficult without the full findings -- what they're arguing is the commission haven't understood it, or that they've misunderstood it and the complexities around the accounting.

This "irrefutable evidence" was what they would've based their arguments when they did the deal with UEFA. It is the same narrative and the same defense they've relied upon. You expect it to have been presented to the Premier League, but the commission rejected it.

Langton: The commission refers to witnesses in support of that evidence, but the witnesses are found in the main to give false and dishonest evidence.

Phillips: Yes, but we don't which witnesses are accused of that, do we?

Langton: Absolutely, we don't know, but they are generally referring to the witness evidence in addition to their irrefutable evidence. For the most part, you would imagine a witness dealing with City's irrefutable evidence would be one of their primary witnesses, but most of those accounts have been found by the commission to be false and dishonest.

Could the appeal be thrown out on grounds it is frivolous?

Phillips: You need proper grounds for the appeal. They'd have to demonstrate, for example, that [the independent commission] had misapplied the law, acted in bad faith, misunderstood the facts, or come to a conclusion that no reasonable commission could possibly have come to. Effectively, that there was some sort of misconduct in the proceedings.

What we've seen from [Man City CEO Ferran] Soriano, is an argument that "we presented all of this evidence. It's irrefutable, but the Premier League have either not considered it or not fully understood it or have been biased."

Given City's legal team, I think they will put together a bunch of grounds that somebody somewhere would have to hold a hearing. But if they mount an appeal without sufficient grounds for a hearing, then there won't be one.

Can City produce new evidence in an appeal?

Phillips: Yes, but it has to be evidence that you can demonstrate wasn't available previously.

How likely is it they will have new evidence?

Phillips: They've had so long to put the case together for these proceedings. I can't imagine something that's happened in the past year or so where they've thought "Oh, we should have presented this," which is why I expect it's all been presented and just been rejected.

So what happens next?

Phillips: There are two ongoing strands to this.

Assuming City appeal as expected, (Editor's note: They have until Friday, Oct. 2 to lodge it.) there's a new three-person independent panel who will be appointed to hear that. On the other hand, you've got the sanction, which would just continue as normal. There would be a sanction hearing, which would be private and if they proceed with the sanction, I think they've got 30 days to then announce what that sanction is.

There's nothing in the Premier League handbook that stops them from moving forward with announcing sanctions, but I think it's another area where you're going to have two competing arguments: one for the Premier League saying "we made a finding" because they have been quite bullish. They're saying, "These are our findings. That's it. Done."

That's why they issued the statement calling the commission's decision the "final award."

Langton: The decision isn't waived because there's an appeal. That is the applicable decision until such time as there is a further decision by the appeal panel.

Phillips: They are under a lot of pressure just to continue with the sanction process, and there's nothing I've seen in the regulations that prevents them from doing so.

Man City, on the other hand, may well argue that it's unfair for them to do that because if they bring about the sanction, it could have an impact, for example, on the impartiality and the decision-making of any appeal. If the sanction were to be a deduction of points, that could impact on their current season. And if they were eventually acquitted, that could have a knock-on effect, which would be, again, unfair on the team.

But would that not confuse the process to proceed to sanction while City were still appealing?

Phillips: That's not uncommon in regulatory or criminal proceedings. If you are convicted of an offense, you can tell the court that you are appealing that conviction, but the judge will just move the sentencing in any case. There are times where they will state really strong grounds for that appeal and it'll make the judge think, "Actually, we need to hear the appeal first." But usually, they'll just proceed to sanction because what they'll see it as is part of the appeal process, right? We can just deal with both.

Let's assume that the appeal fails. What punishments are available to the Premier League? Based on your experience, what is the most likely outcome?

Phillips: There's never been anything on this scale to judge from experience! There'll surely be a substantial fine. The fine needs to reflect not just the breaches, but also the fact they haven't cooperated. So they need to hit them hard with a punitive element, which would be the fine.

A points deduction is something else they can do, and they can also expel them from the Premier League. They can't relegate them, because the Premier League does not have any authority over the English Championship [the second tier] as that is run by the English Football League, but they can hit them with a points deduction so large that they are effectively relegated.

They are going to have to look at this based on the case itself. And as you say, they will consider expulsion or suspension. But, for example, where does suspension leave the current squad of players?

Langton: There's also a balance for the Premier League between the owners, the clubs and the consequences of, let's say, expulsion from the Premier League. If they went down to League Two -- English soccer's fourth and final fully professional tier -- that is going to have an inevitable consequence on all sorts of people who are employed by Manchester City. So there can be unintentional, very serious, adverse consequences for all those people with an expulsion when there is a separation between the owners and the club.

Best educated guess: Do you expect the sanction to come this season?

Phillips: I think the Premier League would want that and I don't see anything that would stop them from doing so, barring a compelling argument from Man City that it would not be right to do so. But if I was to put money on it, I think the sanction would come pretty soon. They are so robust in the findings, saying this is the "final award." [Premier League CEO] Richard Masters is on record saying this is the finding. Why not then sanction?

Can City's current owners continue if the appeal fails? Does any of this meet the threshold for criminal charges? If so, that could potentially lead to an enforced sale?

Phillips: I would need to see the evidence in order to respond. I'm sorry to give you a boring answer like that but when you see the word "dishonesty," I think certainly if there's anybody within this working in the regulated sector, then certainly there are going to be elements of misconduct proceedings that could flow, and possibly criminal charges. You would have to know the extent of the dishonesty per the evidence, but there's no reason why not if they believe a fraud has been committed.

That would then have impact on the owners' test and in the most damaging version, the ownership structure. That test is applied every season. [City CEO] Ferran Soriano, who made the statement this week, has been extremely bullish in his defense. If they don't succeed, you can't see him being around much longer.

Sources have told ESPN that other Premier League clubs are taking legal advice regarding action against City. Can you give us a sense of the scale of the potential associated cases with all this?

Phillips: Other litigation, that is huge. It could come from anyone else in the Premier League who feels impacted -- not just teams that haven't won the league or managed to get into Europe, but every position in the Premier League is worth millions in merit money. You've got teams that were relegated, and individuals who will have faced reputational damage as a result of this. Even ex-City players might even be arguing reputational damage, you just don't know. There could be arguments from teams in Europe that Man City shouldn't have been there.

This just opens up a whole can of worms and everybody will be taking legal advice who has in some way had any sort of impact from what they'll say is Man City cheating.

Finally, where else could City go? We know they cannot go to CAS [the European Court of Arbitration for Sport], but what about the High Court?

Phillips: To go to the High Court, you have to demonstrate that the whole process was unlawful in some way.

Langton: They've already tried to suggest it. That was dealt with in the commission's decision, the argument that the Premier League was outside its jurisdiction and didn't have the ability to bring the charges. And that's been dismissed. So they would be fighting something new.

Phillips: There would need to be strong allegations of fraud that impacted the decision. The tribunal exceeding its powers. They could have a human rights-type argument, that they failed to have a fair hearing, which brings in bias or a lack of impartiality. And then the serious procedural irregularity: the conduct of the proceedings caused substantial injustice. So you can tell from the language here that it's quite a high bar for them to go to the High Court.

And there's nowhere else beyond that?

Phillips: They can't go to CAS [due to Premier League sides agreeing that all issues will be adjudicated under British law, with CAS being a European court]. I guess maybe the Court of Human Rights, if they felt that there was a real unfairness in the proceedings, but the High Court is probably about high as it can go in the UK.

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey schedule hacks: Add more Bruins and Hurricanes to your team
stories.summary: The NHL schedule isn't equal, so use that to your advantage when setting your fantasy hockey lineups in October.
stories.body:
It's never too early to hack the schedule in your fantasy favor, knowing the most effective way to seize an edge on your competition is to maximize every player's opportunity to contribute. By figuring out which teams are more active when most others are not, you seize greater flexibility in boosting your lineup's potential each night. The larger number of players in action on every occasion provides the greater capacity for positive fantasy returns. This advantage hits even harder in tight head-to-head competition, where each point can mean the difference between weekly victory and defeat.

Setting the benchmark at six games, as usual -- when another 20 teams, at minimum, are idle -- a handful of teams are worth recognizing when deciding which available players to keep or stream, all else being equal, on so-called slower nights from Oct. 1 to Oct. 31. The Boston Bruins and Buffalo Sabres lead the way in competing on seven such occasions when most of the rest of the league is off, while a trio of others -- also mentioned below -- do so on six dates. The ability to roll out the following fantasy figures when few others are active, then bench them when off on busier slates, could prove a winning formula in competition where lineups are set every day.

More: Sign up for free | Rankings | Projections | League types

Boston Bruins

One of only two teams to compete on seven lighter dates in October, the Bruins are ripe with streamable options, with winger JJ Peterka leading the way. Rostered in only 41.9% of ESPN Fantasy leagues, the Boston newbie is pegged to skate on a top line and power play with David Pastrnak and Elias Lindholm. One game in, the 24-year-old already has a (very pretty) goal on his 2026-27 resume. After an inferior showing in Utah last year, Peterka is undoubtedly feeling extra motivated to prove himself. Again, keeping on-ice company with Pastrnak also figures largely here.

On the blue line, Hampus Lindholm merits a look in deeper leagues, particularly through the first half of October. When healthy, as he is right now, the veteran defender has a history of riding a 0.41 point/game pace, while firing on net and blocking shots often enough. He's also subbing in on the Bruins' top power play, while Charlie McAvoy rides out his six-game suspension. A worthy streamer in the here and now, Lindholm is overwhelmingly available in ESPN Fantasy competition.

Slotted next to Fraser Minten on the third line and secondary power play, rookie James Hagens could be worth a flier in exceptionally large re-draft leagues. The rookie is at least worth observing while he gets his NHL feet wet, rather than damp. Hagens logged one assist through two regular season games in 2025-26.

Buffalo Sabres

It's fascinating how little fantasy interest the Sabres are garnering altogether, considering how many of their younger players are projected to take a productive leap forward this campaign. For instance, Josh Doan and Zach Benson should both eclipse the 60-point plateau, with goals taking up a good percentage of those points. Ahead of puck-drop, the pair of young men appear slotted in on Buffalo's top power play with Tage Thompson and Rasmus Dahlin.

Looking at the slightly older crowd, the biggest knock on Josh Norris is his inability to remain healthy. While there's no ignoring the forward's too colorful injury history, he's feeling fairly fit right now. If that good fortune lasts through the campaign's first three weeks -- and goodness gracious, hopefully much longer -- he certainly deserves a hard look in all but the shallowest of fantasy leagues. Norris is good for near a point/game when active.

Like the Bruins, Lindy Ruff's crew competes on seven so-called short nights through the first full month of the season.

ESPN Fantasy Hockey is the fun, free way to get inside the game. Draft your players, set your lineups and earn points when the pros do. Sign up today!

Anaheim Ducks

Not only do they play on six occasions when most of the league is off, but five of those tilts are at home, where the Ducks strung together a 24-13-4 record this past season. Beyond Cutter Gauthier, Leo Carlsson and Beckett Sennecke - who are all likely spoken for in the majority of ESPN leagues -- Mikael Granlund merits consideration as a streamer or injury substitute to launch 2026-27. The freshly-minted captain is competing on Anaheim's top power play along with the secondary scoring line. Available in nearly 40% of ESPN leagues, he'll put up a reasonable number of points.

Otherwise, keep an eye on A.J. Greer. Coach Joel Quenneville recently offered the former Panther a practice turn on the Ducks' top line with Carlsson and Gauthier. An interesting idea, after Greer "erupted" (it's all relative) for 17 goals and 15 assists in 78 games this past season. It certainly doesn't hurt to stay on top of the situation, particularly in deeper fantasy leagues.

As for between the pipes, I'm wary to endorse Lukas Dostal with the Ducks' refurbished defense in place. Let's first place the talented goalie on the wait-and-see shelf and give the inexperienced blue line an opportunity to surprise.

Calgary Flames

While Calgary's roster isn't exactly crowded with high-end fantasy talent, it also isn't fully devoid. Since someone needs to score for the Flames, Matt Coronato projects as the early choice to lead that list of someones. Entering his third full NHL season, the top-line winger sports 30-goal/30-assist potential.

After putting up 20 points in 37 games his first season, Matvei Gridin -- Coronato's linemate on the top unit and No. 1 power play -- serves as a true fantasy wild card at age 20. The first-round draft selection (2024) made even more productive noise in his AHL run with the Wranglers. Also entering his first full campaign with the Flames, defender Zayne Parekh is forecast to lead the blue line in production, particularly with the extra skater. I realize we're focusing on potential here, but rebuilding or not, the Flames are still going to put points on the board.

No rush here though. Despite suiting up on six lighter dates total, Calgary's schedule doesn't really deserve hacking until the final week of the month, when the club faces the Toronto Leafs, Edmonton Oilers and Seattle Kraken on exceptionally light nights (they also play the Colorado Avalanche on a busier Saturday). Flag your favorite fantasy Flames in the meanwhile.

Made it this far? Create your own league with your own rules and play against your friends today.

Carolina Hurricanes

Check your wire to see if Jackson Blake, Logan Stankoven or Taylor Hall is available. Then consider picking up one of them, in that prioritized order, for the first two full weeks of October, at minimum. After battling the Washington Capitals and Philadelphia Flyers Oct. 2 and 3, the Hurricanes play the Montreal Canadiens, Vancouver Canucks, Chicago Blackhawks and Philly (again) the next week. A friendly enough schedule. Tilts with Washington, Winnipeg and Calgary follow that stretch, with the Flames' date falling on a Sunday featuring only one other NHL contest.

Considering how productive they were in the postseason (combing for 55 points in 19 games) I'm surprised at the lackluster fantasy interest in this trio. Blake is 23 years old, Stankoven is 22, and even Hall is proving he's still got plenty in the tank at 34. The playoff performance from this dynamite scoring line doesn't feel flukey in the slightest.

At the opposing end of the busy-night spectrum, the Maple Leafs, Vegas Golden Knights, Capitals and Winnipeg Jets play only once when most of the rest of the league is off.

stories.headline: Spurs' Victor Wembanyama not interested in promoting betting sites
stories.summary: Spurs star Victor Wembanyama said Thursday that he isn't interested in promoting sports betting sites.
stories.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- Count Spurs star Victor Wembanyama as one of the professional athletes who isn't interested in promoting sports betting sites.

The Frenchman expressed his view on the subject Thursday after a training camp workout.

"Absolutely not," Wembanyama said when asked if he'd ever consider promoting a sports betting website. "I will never do that. Honestly, I think it's very sad to see some players promote it. Everybody does whatever they want, but without me."

Wembanyama was subsequently asked how he makes decisions about which brands to promote.

"In the past, there was a dimension of money," he said. "Not anymore. Even if I said that, I've refused plenty, much, much more money than I've made for things that were not [in line with] my values. And now, I want to promote things that have a good impact, have a good influence with who I can share messages and values. Obviously, we earn millions and millions. This is not our biggest strength. Our biggest strength is inspiring. I want to inspire in a good way. That's the strongest thing I can do."

Several of Wembanyama's NBA peers currently promote sportsbooks and prediction platforms, including LeBron James, who moved from DraftKings to Polymarket in September, Kevin Durant (FanDuel), who is also an investor in Kalshi and Giannis Antetokounmpo, who became a shareholder at Kalshi back in February.

"The internet is full of opinions," Antetokounmpo wrote in a since-deleted post on X, announcing the move. "I decided it was time to make some of my own. Today, I'm joining Kalshi as a shareholder."

Three-time MVP Nikola Jokic, in 2023, became the first brand ambassador of Superbet in Serbia.

The NBA's collective bargaining agreement treats sports betting operators and prediction markets the same when it comes down to player partnerships. Players aren't allowed to promote betting on any market related to the NBA. But they are allowed to endorse and hold de minimis equity investments in sports betting companies with some restrictions.

Wembanyama, meanwhile, enters his fourth season in the league coming off San Antonio's first appearance in the NBA Finals since 2014. The two-time All-Star last season became the first player to unanimously win NBA Defensive Player of the Year after leading the league in blocks for the third-consecutive season.

Wembanyama, 22, finished third last season in voting for NBA MVP.

stories.headline: Source: Diamondbacks to retain Torey Lovullo as manager
stories.summary: Torey Lovullo, the winningest manager in Diamondbacks history over his 10 seasons, will be returning on a new contract, a source told ESPN.
stories.body:
The Arizona Diamondbacks are bringing back Torey Lovullo, the winningest manager in franchise history, a source told ESPN's Alden Gonzalez on Thursday.

Lovullo, 61, whose deal expired after this season, will receive a new two-year contract, the Arizona Republic reported.

Lovullo's future with the club was in flux after the Diamondbacks missed the playoffs for a third straight year. Arizona was eliminated from postseason contention on the final day of the regular season for the second time in three seasons when the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Tampa Bay Rays 7-4 on Sunday.

The D-backs finished with an 86-76 record -- the best in MLB for a team that didn't qualify for October baseball.

"I want to win a world championship with this organization, but I want to be wanted," Lovullo said after the final game of the regular season. "... I'll leave it at that."

He said earlier this month that he thought the Diamondbacks needed to make the playoffs for him and his coaching staff to return next season.

Diamondbacks president Derrick Hall recently said he thinks Lovullo likely did the best managing job of his career this season while Arizona struggled with major injuries and distractions that included the latest bizarre absence of star Ketel Marte in August.

Lovullo has gone 750-768 during a full decade in charge, with the highlight being a surprise World Series appearance in 2023. He is the third-longest-tenured manager in the big leagues behind Tampa Bay's Kevin Cash and Los Angeles Dodgers skipper Dave Roberts.

The affable Lovullo is a popular presence in the organization. He played eight seasons in the big leagues for seven teams in the 1980s and 1990s. He was the bench coach for the Boston Red Sox when they won the World Series in 2013 and played college baseball at UCLA.

"Arizona is my home," Lovullo said after the final game of the season. "I love Arizona, and the people and the fans are spectacular. The group that I work for is amazing. I love being around them every single day, and I don't want that to change."

Lovullo was hired as Arizona's manager four weeks after Hazen took over as general manager, and their tenures are still intertwined. Their Diamondbacks have had the misfortune to be in the National League West with the dominant Dodgers, who have won 13 of the last 14 division titles -- and with the San Diego Padres, who have made the postseason in five of the past seven years during the best stretch in franchise history.

Arizona, however, hasn't been able to snare a wild-card berth despite rosters full of veteran talent and a solid young core, repeatedly falling just short at big moments.

The Diamondbacks started this season with postseason expectations and were in contention throughout the summer, but the team could never quite reach its full potential. Two of the team's main starting pitchers -- Zac Gallen and Merrill Kelly -- struggled and injuries to ace right-hander Corbin Burnes, relievers A.J. Puk and Justin Martinez, and top prospect Jordan Lawlar put a dent in their depth.

Catcher Gabriel Moreno won the NL batting title this season, but other key hitters like Marte, Corbin Carroll and Geraldo Perdomo were inconsistent.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton hits out at Ferrari hierarchy in Fred Vasseur defence: 'Point fingers somewhere else'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has reiterated his full support for Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur and said critics should "point fingers somewhere else," suggesting those higher up in the team's hierarchy must also take responsibility for its struggles.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has reiterated his full support for Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur and said critics should "point fingers somewhere else," suggesting those higher up in the team's hierarchy must also take responsibility for its struggles.

Vasseur's job has come under increasing scrutiny over the past month, with reports last week linking ex-Red Bull boss Christian Horner to replace him.

The speculation grew so much Ferrari felt the need this week to clarify that Ferrari's corporate leadership has "full confidence" in Vasseur, albeit via a press conference with the team's head of communications and not through a statement from either company CEO Benedetto Vigna or chairman John Elkann.

"Ultimately, it's not a one-man operation," Hamilton said in a passionate defence of his team boss to TV in Malaysia on Thursday. "If you want to point fingers, point them somewhere else. There are lot of people above that also are a part of it.

"So if you want to take something from this message: Fred's in his position, he's not going anywhere and I'm here to stay with him. And I still believe fully in where we're going."

Speaking to the written media afterwards, Hamilton reiterated: "I think Fred has the full backing.

"There often seems to be a lot of focus on one individual in one role here. And you can see that, obviously, they've switched out lots of different people in Fred's role. But Fred is a fantastic leader.

"He really is the guy to take his team in the right direction. However, there is a structure that's been there for some time. Whether or not that needs looking at moving forward, there are obviously also people above Fred, and it's not about one person.

"Fred has led the team to ... He's helped make changes in this past year, he's helped us get to the second in the constructors' championship. That's a huge step from last year."

Hamilton was then asked if one of the issues Ferrari has is that Vasseur has no financial stake in the race team, unlike his former boss Toto Wolff, who oversees all facets of the Mercedes F1 team.

In reply to whether Ferrari could benefit with a similar structure to Mercedes, Hamilton said: "There are changes that I would make, but I'm not going to talk about what those are. Toto's in a different position to Fred. The structure's a lot different. That's all I can say."

Ferrari has always been subjected to intense scrutiny, attention which has likely only increased the longer the team's title drought has gone on -- the team's last constructors' title was 2008, with its last drivers' title in 2007.

- Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: Where were today's drivers when F1 last raced at Sepang?

- Max Verstappen steps in for GT race at Portimão amid two F1 triple-headers

Hamilton said the recent reporting about the state of the internals of the team have been wide of the market.

"For me, it's frustrating to see all the negativity. Because you see other people making mistakes, and they don't normally say too much about them," he said.

"We either make the same mistake, or are not perfect and and it's ten times worse for some reason for Ferrari, but that's also to be expected. Given that it's the best brand here, it's the most iconic by far. For me, I don't read a lot, so that has zero effect on me. But of course, when I come into the room and see, it definitely affects individuals on the team.

"Because every weekend they try and show up and do the best job they can, and they don't get it right all the time. Families are messaging you for all the negative things that they're reading when the people back at the factory are reading all those things, even though they're giving their all. It's almost like sometimes you feel like there's nothing you can do right, even when you're giving your all.

"For me, the message is to not read any of the stuff that's being written. Because the fact is, nobody that's writing any of the stuff has actually any clue what they're talking about, because they're not in the team.

"They don't know what's happening behind closed doors. They don't know how hard everybody's working. It's all down to assumptions and opinions."

Vasseur and Hamilton worked together back in Formula 2 before being reunited at Ferrari.

"Fred's been fantastic working with me and I think our relationship as a whole -- even with our bosses -- is in a better place than it ever was," he added to television.

"Fred's made a lot of changes I've asked for already. I think it's not an easy time for Fred so I think it's good that the team came out with that earlier this week. I've also let him know I support him 100%.

"I wouldn't be here without Fred. Swapping him out ... it won't change how the team moves forwards. It would be detrimental to it."

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Thursday, Oct. 1

Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Philadelphia Union, USMNT's Cavan Sullivan becomes youngest MLS Player of the Month
stories.summary: Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.
stories.body:
Philadelphia Union and United States men's national team midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.

At 16, Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player to start a game for the United States since Freddy Adu in 2006 when he was picked in Mauricio Pochettino's XI for Saturday's 4-1 friendly win vs. Peru.

He was one of 11 players -- including seven other teenagers -- to make their first appearances for the U.S. in that game against Peru.

Sullivan, who turned 17 on Sept. 28, came on as a substitute on Tuesday in the USMNT's 4-2 friendly win over Chile.

Sullivan has seven goals and 12 assists in 26 games for the Union, who have surged up to sixth place in the Eastern Conference in recent weeks. He has played 1,675 league minutes in MLS.

His 19 goal contributions are tied with Alphonso Davies (2018) for the second-most by a teenager in an MLS season, trailing only Diego Fagundez (20 in 2013).

Since returning from the World Cup break, the Union have recorded 32 points during a 12-game unbeaten streak, which is tied for the most points by a club in a 12-game span in MLS history. Sullivan has started all 11 of those games, logging a goal contribution in eight of them.

Sullivan and the Union will return after the FIFA international break on Oc. 10 to host Real Salt Lake at Subaru Park (7:30 p.m. ET).

stories.headline: Roosters star admits he is torn on World Cup decision
stories.summary: Robert Toia has revealed he is still undecided if he wants to play for Australia or Tonga in the World Cup, less than a week out from teams being named.
stories.body:
Robert Toia has admitted he still doesn't know who he wants to play for at the World Cup, as the in-demand centre weighs up representing Tonga or Australia.

Toia is the highest-profile player caught in a tug-of-war between nations, with the World Cup just a fortnight ago and final squads to be announced next week.

Tonga coach Kristian Woolf had told AAP this week that Toia had indicated he wanted to represent the Pacific nation, after debuting for them last year.

Australia counterpart Kevin Walters has also made clear he believes the Sydney Roosters star is available for the Kangaroos, and he has not been told otherwise.

Toia has accepted he must make a decision soon, but remains uncertain what way he will go with Sunday's NRL grand final against Newcastle before this month's tournament.

"To be honest, I have not made my mind up," Toia told AAP.

"I just find it hard that I don't have a decision. I want to play for Tonga, it means so much to my family, myself and my people.

"I went over to Tonga last year and you can see how much it means to them.

"But to have Australia on your resume. Just to play for Australia, in my second year, I find it such a massive achievement. That's what I'm kind of weighing up."

Beyond Toia, Woolf also believes Sydney Roosters teammates Salesi Foketi and Siua Wong want to play for Tonga in the global showpiece.

Queensland winger Jojo Fifita revealed this week he too was still undecided, weighing up whether to play for Australia, New Zealand or Tonga.

Fifita told AAP he'd had discussions with all three nations, although he was not named in the Kiwis' initial 40-man squad.

Walters has said both Jojo and his brother David are under consideration for Australia's World Cup squad.

In better news for Tonga, Dolphins halfback Isaiya Katoa has confirmed he will be fit for the tournament after a syndesmosis injury in the preliminary-final loss to the Roosters.

"I don't need surgery. I will be able to play in the World Cup," Katoa said.

"I immediately knew I had done something, so I was definitely happy once I got the scans back it wasn't too bad and I will be able to represent Tonga."

Complicating matters for players who are weighing up their future is the fact Australian representatives stand to earn $40,000 by playing in the tournament.

AAP is aware of coaches and players who are concerned that may prompt some players to choose the Kangaroos in order to benefit their families.

But Katoa said it would never be a factor for him.

"I'd never look at the price tag, it's always where my heart is at," he said.

"I've always said my heart is at Tonga and if it wasn't for Tonga I am half-Cook Islands as well. So if it wasn't for Tonga, I would go Cook Islands."

Meanwhile it is understood Tonga will pick former St George Illawarra half Talatau Amone in their squad for the tournament.

Amone has not played since he was deregistered by the NRL in 2023 for assault. Tonga are still yet to learn if he will be cleared to play in the tournament.

He can return to the NRL next year, and starred on his return to Queensland Cup with Wynnum-Manly in recent months.
